title: Stages of the second birth
steps: Immaculate conception (ἄμωμος σύλληψις), ineffable, below senses and mind
Gestation (κυοφορία) of logos and virtue, losing veils while being nourished
Labour and birth (γέννα) 'suddenly', with a midwife-teacher
Nourishment and strengthening (θρέψις, ῥῶσις) by starlight and moonlight
Beholding the Sun of the Good itself
note: The order follows a real pregnancy: nothing can be skipped, the newborn must be protected and fed, and only a stabilised soul can look at the Sun.

title: Three stages of initiation
steps: Conception (σύλληψη)
Gestation (κυοφορία)
Birth (γένεση)
note: Initiation (μύησις) is pregnancy (κύησις): what is conceived must be carried before it is born.

title: The ascent out of the Cave
steps: Seeing shadows: 'it seems, but it is not'
Sudden release and turning around: gestation, confusion, being called mad
Approaching the exit, dazzled: the longest night, labour
Pulled out by a helper: birth in the place of the Good
Starlight and moonlight, then strengthening, then the Sun itself
Pushed back down to awaken others
note: Each step of Plato's allegory is a stage of the soul's pregnancy and birth, ending with the return.

title: Three grades of the Socratic saying
steps: 'I know that I do not know' (deconstruction)
'I saw the One that is nothing' (birth)
'I saw that I saw nothing' (beholding the Sun beyond the One)
note: Her reconstruction: emptying leads to birth, and birth to the vision beyond even the One. The wording is garbled in the transcript.

title: Two movements of philosophy
steps: Transcendence (ὑπέρβασις): close the eyes, turn away, find the One beyond
Immanence (ἐμμένεια): return to the cave and see the One remain in all
note: Proclus' procession and return; the second movement takes longer and completes the cycle.

title: Persephone's three names
steps: Bearer of death (φέρουσα φόνον)
Bearer of light (Φερσέφασσα)
Bearer of touch (Φερέπαφα)
note: The soul first dies into the body, then carries the light, then touches the immortal and returns home.

title: Out of forgetting: Leto's births
steps: Flight from Lethe
Artemis (virtue, ἀρετή)
Apollo on Delos (manifest light)
note: Virtue comes before truth becomes manifest.

title: Diotima's ladder of eros
steps: Bodily attraction
Attraction of souls
Political eros: love of society, its laws and people
Eros of the sciences
Eros of the arts
Absolute or divine eros: merging into the ocean of life
note: She speaks of 'seven steps' but names about six; love widens from bodies to the whole until it is union with the divine. In Part B she places the erotic union with the One at the final step.

title: Plato's three similes
steps: Sun
Line
Cave
note: The Sun comes first to give a key for ἀναγωγή, the ascent from the sensible to the intelligible; the Cave then summarises the whole path.

title: Levels of justice mapped onto the Cave
steps: Deep cave (φαίνεσθαι): the court system
Middle cave (γίγνεσθαι): retributive give-and-take (Polemarchus: pay your debts)
Inner key: τὰ ἑαυτοῦ πράττειν, doing one's own from the fiery Self
Beyond the cave: the finest, fastest fire passing through all things
note: Justice deepens from institutions to exchange to the soul's constitution to the cosmic fire.

title: How the freed one learns to see
steps: Reflections in water and the 'astral field'
The sun itself
note: Like walking from a dark basement into an Aegean summer, the eyes must adjust in stages.

title: Intention, position, vision
steps: Intention (πρόθεσις)
Position (θέσις)
Vision (θέασις)
note: Each determines the next, so she begins any teaching by stating her intention.

title: The emanation ladder
steps: The One (ἕν), wholly transcendent
The Monad (μονάς), source of outflow
Nous, the first emanation
Soul, cooled nous
Matter
note: One continuum drawn as a sphere: everything happens inside the One, nothing is cut off.

title: The chain of vehicles
steps: Body, vehicle of the soul
Soul, vehicle of nous
Nous, vehicle of the fire
note: Each layer is worn by the one within; self-knowledge recognises the fire that wears them all.

title: The four cardinal days of the year
steps: Winter solstice (22 December)
Spring equinox (21 March)
Summer solstice (21-22 June)
Autumn equinox (21 September), climax of the Eleusinian Mysteries
note: Ancient Greek festivals were organised around these days of highest energetic inflow.

title: From βίος to ζωή to εὖ ζῆν
steps: βίος: instinctive, mechanical survival
ζωή: life warmed by ζέσις and lit by νοῦς
εὖ ζῆν: life joined to the Good
note: Βίος becomes ζωή when we activate νόησις and λόγος and follow the 'deep heartbeat'; adding εὖ makes it the good life.

title: How knowledge is born
steps: Conceive a seed or idea
Carry it and give it time
Deliver it with maieutic help
note: Information is received; knowledge must be gestated and born in you, moved by love.

title: Stages of the Cave
steps: Chained deep in the cave, facing the wall of shadows
Freed, confused about what is real
Dragged up the rough, steep ascent, eyes burning
Seeing by night, by the stars
Seeing by day
Seeing the sun itself, the Good
Returning down out of compassion
note: The stages map onto the soul before paideia, the process of paideia and its result, freedom and illumination; the return completes the path.

title: The three marks of awakening
steps: Universal, impersonal love
εὐθυμία: childlike cheer, seeing life as divine play
Indifference to ego-centred goals; serving the One and all beings
note: These replace false signs like aura, diet, vocabulary or lifestyle; they follow from the separate self falling away.

title: The four attributes of the One
steps: ἄρρητον (árrhēton): ineffable
ἄγνωστον (ágnōston): unknowable
ἄληπτον (álēpton): ungraspable
ἀμέθεκτον (améthekton): unparticipated, 'does not mix'
note: Each is a negation: the One can only be approached apophatically. Everything is in it and it is in everything, yet it is outside every 'something'.

title: The three-in-one jackpot
steps: A ripened desire for freedom in the soul
Access to a teaching
A gathering (ὁμήγυρις) of companions with the same desire
note: Tradition calls this meeting of desire, method and company a rare, blessed conjuncture, and the reason to begin with gratitude.

title: Her three-level method for reading the Cave
steps: External: political, the senses, 'where is the cave out there'
Internal: the cave within, read through ontology, epistemology and psychology
Mystical or innermost: no inside or outside, only the One
note: Like an atom or an onion, each layer lies deeper; she counts five levels in all, justified by Homer's 'all things are divided in three'.

title: The lineage she traces
steps: Orpheus (thousands of years ago, not about 1200 BCE)
Pythagoras
Socrates
Plato
Aristotle
Plotinus
Iamblichus
Proclus
Damascius, last scholarch at Justinian's edict
note: Philosophy as a path of awakening passed down a living line; connecting to this root lets blessings and knowledge flow.

title: The three allegories of Republic VI-VII
steps: The Sun
The Divided Line
The Cave
note: The Cave comes third and completes the picture, showing the human before, during and after paideia.

title: The four turnings of the year
steps: Winter solstice, 21 or 22 December (Capricorn)
Spring equinox, about 21 March (Aries)
Summer solstice, about 21 June (Cancer)
Autumn equinox, 21 September (Libra), culmination of the Eleusinian Mysteries
note: Aries, Cancer, Libra and Capricorn are signs 1, 4, 7 and 10, a Pythagorean series. They are energy gates, but the best moment is always now.

title: How sensation happens (Timaeus 43a-c)
steps: The river's surging wave flows in and out through the soul's circles
The body strikes external fire, earth, water or air
These collisions set up motions carried through the body
The motions strike and buffet the soul's circles
The soul receives them passively as παθήματα
These motions are named sensations (αἰσθήσεις)
note: The organs are only gates: it is the soul, its nous, that senses, which is why a body without a soul feels nothing.

title: From the newborn's confusion to phronesis
steps: Newborn: the Same and the Other are twisted, the world upside down
The inflow of growth loses its first force
The soul's motions 'take advantage of the calm' (γαλήνη)
The circles resume their course and strengthen
Judgment of same and different becomes correct
The person is on the road to φρόνησις
note: How far we develop judgment depends on how we use our senses and relate the river's motions to the soul's.

title: From seeing to deification
steps: A change of θέασις (seeing)
θέωσις (deification)
Awakening and eudaimonia
note: Paideia is the art of turning the soul's gaze; changing how we see is what transforms us.

title: The 'why' chain to eudaimonia
steps: Any choice: the car, the marriage, the job
Why? For creativity, excellence, security
Why? To relax at last in the present
To enjoy the here and now of eternity
Eudaimonia, today called awakening or enlightenment
note: Aristotle's point: eudaimonia is the final cause of every act, with nothing behind it.

title: Winter solstice inner work
steps: Turn inward: darkness means introversion
Descend like Persephone with the hero's torch
Face your monsters and hidden passions
Trace their roots in events, family dynamics and ancestors
Uproot them and light them with awareness
Sow virtue, love, kindness, cooperation and truth
At rock bottom, choose 'light or nothing'
The inner sun is born
note: Descent is the condition of the inner birth; trauma can become θαῦμα.

title: The solstice birth days
steps: 21 or 22 December: the solstice
22 to 24 December: the sun appears to 'stand' (the triple night)
25 December: Ἡλιούγεννα, the birth of the sun
note: The hero is thrice sown, gestated and born before the sun's birth.

title: From sowing to birth
steps: Autumn equinox: the Eleusinian Mysteries, a sowing
Nine months of gestation
Summer solstice: the birth
note: Equinoxes are spiritual sowings that lead to psychic pregnancies and, in time, births.

title: The Moon's three faces
steps: Hecate
Artemis
Athena, the highest, 'returning' face
note: Her own triadic reading of the lunar faces.

title: The three lights
steps: Sensible light (ἡλ-, as in ἥλιος)
Spiritual light (ἑλ-, as in Ἕλλην)
Uncreated light (third root uncertain)
note: Light rises from the visible sun to spirit to the uncreated.

title: Plotinus' marks of eternity (Ennead III.7)
steps: ἀτρεμής: untrembling (she links it to Artemis)
ὁμοῦ πᾶσα: all together
ἀκλινής: without inclination
ἐν ἑνὶ ἑστῶσα: standing in the one
note: Eternity does not tilt or tremble; standing toward the One is being present.

title: Knowledge as a vehicle
steps: Ignorance
Knowledge: the car, the bridge
Getting out of the car and walking
The dive into lived experience of the One
note: Knowledge lies between ignorance and awakening; some people stay in the car forever.

title: Her own path
steps: Gibran's The Prophet at about 13
Plato's Euthyphro and the Forms at 14
The Republic with Janet Coleman at LSE
Autobiography of a Yogi in 2008, at about 23
Oxford by day, many hours of meditation
A month alone in India: the heart opens
A realisation of oneness
note: Realisation added up step by step, until it culminated in seeing one ocean of consciousness.

title: The ladder of virtues
steps: Political or ethical virtues: remove negative habits and purify passions such as greed, jealousy and anger
Cathartic virtues: diet, mantras, energy work, purifying the luminous body
Theoretical virtues: mathematics, the Ideas, dialectics, taught only after preparation
Paradigmatic virtues: transmissions from teacher to student through energy, symbolic objects or phrases
Theurgic virtues: rites and Mysteries that unify and bring sudden revelation
note: Virtues are habits of being in grades; theory comes only after purification, and the summit is unification beyond words.

title: The four pillars of Pythagorean method
steps: Epistemic pillar: train intellect and critical thinking to clear biases and dogmas
Ethical, cathartic and political pillar: cultivate heart, compassion and right motivation for the common good
Initiation: contemplation, ritual, meditation, sleep yoga
Guidance of the perfected soul into union, drawing from the inner hearth of light
note: The mind is healed first so the soul can open; she first said five steps, then counted four.

title: The temple of the self
steps: Entrance (pronaos): the outer self of body, mind, personality and life story
Main hall with the god's statue: the inner self, the soul and its faculties of mind, heart, will and appetite
Inner sanctum (ἄδυτον, ἄβατον): the secret self, oneself as the One
note: Knowing yourself moves inward through the temple, from the story of the small self to the true nature of being.

title: The non-dual cascade of being
steps: The unknowable One (ἄγνωστον), before awareness
Νοῦς, awareness, emanated through Eros
Ψυχή, localised and cooled energy
Matter, projected by soul
note: Nested like a babushka doll: a continuum, not a duality of mind and matter. She gives the same cascade, via Heraclitus, in the Chitheads talk (drptI20Rf5k, 36:52).

title: The cave as a map of mind
steps: Impressions
Emotional feeling tones
Concepts and ideas
Awareness
note: The cave lays out the structure of consciousness, which she turns into embodied meditations.

title: The golden thread
steps: Orpheus, founder of the mysteries
The Presocratics
Pythagoras
Socrates
Plato
The Stoics
The Neoplatonists
Cut by Justinian's decree in 529 AD
note: One tradition with many branches, ended by force and leaving texts without practices.

title: Diotima's ladder of eros, as she tells it
steps: Interpersonal attraction, bodily or psychic
Loving a partner or family: ceasing to be an ἰδιώτης
Beyond oneself and one's own (she calls this the fourth grade)
Political eros: love of the city's values, institutions and laws
Cosmic love: recognising the unity of all
note: She counts seven levels in total but names only these; the opening goes from private to political to cosmic.

title: The eros of the question
steps: Turn attention inward and ask who am I
Each question opens a space within
Recognise the soul beyond personality and body
In time, recognise νοῦς, your consciousness
Taste that consciousness is one and common
Recognise that unity as love
note: Questioning is itself erotic: it leads to the all of the answer.

title: From love to eudaimonia
steps: Learn to practise love in daily life
Cultivate virtue
Reach eudaimonia
note: Diotima's education: love is the method, virtue the fruit, eudaimonia the end.

title: Three stages of Hellenic meditation
steps: Στοχασμός: place one object at the centre of consciousness and study it inwardly, like a thought experiment
Διαλογισμός: let awareness expand through the field of your intention until something is conceived
Θεωρία: subject, object and process merge into one
note: From focus to expansion to non-dual merging; the third term was not clearly captured.

title: The cure for Greece
steps: Cooperate with Athena: ethics, self-knowledge, philosophy, serious study
Drink again from Homer's spring with fresh Greek eyes
Return to Ithaca, the origin, not nostalgically
Slay the suitors who would appropriate the heritage
Rebuild Greekness on archetypal pillars
Bring the sites to life and make Greece a centre of research
note: The collective healing follows the plot of the Odyssey.

title: The last five Orphic hymns
steps: Hestia (84): essence
Sleep (85)
Dream (86)
Death (87)
Ares the Warrior (88)
note: Essence falls asleep, dreams incarnation, the dream ends, and at once the impulse of birth returns: every end is a beginning.

title: Pisces to Aries
steps: Pisces, the 12th sign: death
Aries, the 1st sign: birth at the spring equinox
note: The two signs border each other, so the cycle closes: 'every end of mine is my beginning'.

title: The rainbow of the world
steps: God is light
Split into seven colours, light forms the seven strata of the world
1 and 2 are principles; 3 to 9 are the seven levels
Red, the outermost band, is matter and Ares
Wisdom stands at the centre
note: Our centre should be wisdom, but our edges must be red: every creation needs guarded boundaries.

title: Raising Ares
steps: Lay a base of purity (ἀγνότης)
The red fire stops being Plato's black horse
It is transmuted and rises like kundalini
It brings fearlessness and ἀνδρεία
It crowns the head as the golden helmet (χρυσεοπήληξ)
note: Raised vital force turns out to be a dense distillate of solar quintessence; without purity it degrades into lower Ares.

title: Out of the cave
steps: The prisoners spontaneously decide to stand up: 'it can't be only this'
They wander the cave and meet one already freed
The guide pulls them out to the light
Their eyes burn and adjust
They see birds and trees
Finally they see the sun of the Good, the One
note: Free will moves first; help comes after; seeing is gradual.

title: Ignorance, illusion, knowledge
steps: Total ignorance
The world of phenomena: an intermediate illusion
Knowledge and truth
note: The visible world is not nothing; it is a middle stage between ignorance and truth.

title: Two stages of γνῶθι σαυτόν
steps: Know your preferences, personality, body, mind, heart and desires: the three parts of the soul
Know 'that which knows': the observer itself
note: The first stage is valid but Apollo asks more: you are not what you have.

title: What the philosopher dies from
steps: The body
The psychic field behind phenomena
The world of consciousness, the intelligible place
A last step beyond even consciousness, to what truly is
note: Dis-identification proceeds level by level until nothing one has is mistaken for what one is.

title: The three levels of the cave
steps: Sleep or ignorance: full identification with the body
Becoming: apprenticeship, pregnancy, initiation (?)
Awakening: the realm of Being under the sun of the Good
note: The middle stage is the womb in which the second birth is gestated.

title: Philosophy in two movements
steps: Death of the illusory self
Rebirth into Being, then return
note: Equivalently: apprenticeship, then the stable establishment of eudaimonia in daily life.

title: The aim of the Pythagorean school
steps: Purification from the mortal body (and material irrationality (?))
Purification from the passions
Perfection through virtue, leading to eudaimonia
Ascent (ἀναγωγή) to likeness with the divine (ὁμοίωσις θεῷ)
note: The last step is awakening to the oneness of my essence and the universe's essence.

title: Four stages of Pythagorean paideia
steps: Train ὀρθὸς λόγος: clarity and observation, telling true from false and harmonious from disharmonious
Cultivate the virtues through ἦθος as habituation, above all love
Initiation (μύησις) into the natural, psychic and spiritual powers
Illumination and union
note: Love is the hinge: without love of self, beings, wisdom and the whole, no awakening is possible.

title: The four Pythagorean principles
steps: Our nature and the divine essence are eternal: we are the One ('Unity is the law of God')
The One divides into parts, and from parts comes μοῖρα ('Number is the law of the universe')
Incarnating without παιδεία we drink Lethe, identify with the part, and suffer
There is a way out, the path of awakening ('Evolution is the law of life')
note: A diagnosis and a cure: unity, division, forgetting, return.

title: The three rooms of a Greek temple
steps: Πρόναος (vestibule): exoteric meaning
Σηκός (main hall with the statue): esoteric meaning
Ἄδυτον / ἄβατον (priests only): apocryphal, unspeakable meaning
note: The last level goes beyond mind and is grasped only through pure experience, 'witness'.

title: The path ahead in the Pythagoras cycle
steps: Catharsis
Virtues
Right seeing (ὀρθὴ θέασις)
Knowledge
Initiation
note: Each stage has practices for settling the right inner 'tonalities'.

title: Make music, then work
steps: Tune the soul's frequencies into harmony (virtue)
Harmony becomes a gate to the One
Return and embody the realisation as work
note: Awakening is incomplete until it is built into individual and collective life.

title: Stages of self-knowledge
steps: Decide: 'I want to know myself', and shift focus inward
Know yourself not as body but as soul: desiring, feeling, thinking
Observe these continuously: an 'extremely therapeutic' stage
Become an active maker of your character
Ask who the pure essence is from which the three powers arise
note: Observation restores the soul's free flow, which is virtue, before the final question.

title: Plato's three parts of the soul, in her order
steps: τὸ ἐπιθυμητικόν: all our desires
τὸ θυμοειδές: heart and emotions
τὸ λογιστικόν: mind and thoughts
note: These are powers of the soul, not the soul itself, as melody is not the kithara.

title: The parts of ἐλευθερία
steps: Ἑλ: light, the sense of unity with all
εὖ: the good, as good person and good citizen
θερ- read as ἔρως: the love that warms and leads to the whole
note: Her 'onomatological axis' of the talk: freedom is light, the good and eros; she admits she slips an omega under an omicron.

title: How the hero becomes eternal
steps: Defy death: 'I do not care for my own hide'
So dis-identify from the ego
So become one with all
The all was, is and will be
So one has become eternal: how could one die?
note: Heroic immortality is a state of consciousness, not the soul's immortality, which we already have.

title: From «No» to civilisation
steps: Say «No» to vice and the ego
Attune to the common logos
Return
Say «Yes»: build value, social and political foundations
A civilisation blossoms as a pole of attraction for later generations
note: This is her picture of the ancient Greek idea of politics; «No» and «Yes» should cycle forever.

title: Apollo's five steps of awakening and their four passages
steps: Step 1, Πύθιος (Pythios): beginners who learn and inquire; the restless prisoner asks while old, rotten forces still hold the soul's oracle
Passage 1, ἀπολούων (washing): Apollo the healer cleanses what we thought we knew; it starts with the will to change
Step 2, Δήλιος (Delios): truth declared through a medium, as signs and synchronicities, like birth pangs
Passage 2, ἁπλοῦς (simple): mantic; the many opinions fall away and simple truth is known without medium
Step 3, Φαναῖος (Phanaios): direct glimpses of the One, the veil pierced for an instant
Passage 3, ἀεὶ βάλλων (ever-shooting): the archer; the will stops changing and holds one target
Step 4, Ἰσμήνιος (Ismenios): those who have knowledge, 'we know' and 'we are'; out of the cave and into mystical education
Passage 4, ὁμοπολῶν (moving the poles together): music; returning to the many to harmonise opposites, the political step
Step 5, Λεσχηνόριος (Leschenorios): dialogue and philosophy shared for the common good; life as a feast
note: Five steps have four intervals, so each Cratylus etymology is the passage between two of Plutarch's names; together they make nine keys, the ennead or 'new one'. Plutarch names Delios and Phanaios together for one group of seekers; making them two separate steps is her own reading.

title: Plutarch's five names of Apollo, in her order
steps: Πύθιος (Pythios): for those beginning to learn and inquire
Δήλιος (Delios): truth declared through signs
Φαναῖος (Phanaios): truth shining through directly
Ἰσμήνιος (Ismenios): for those who have knowledge
Λεσχηνόριος (Leschenorios): for those who enjoy dialogue and philosophising together
note: Plutarch, following his teacher Ammonius, matches each name to the seeker's condition: the god appears according to our state. He gives Delios and Phanaios together; she separates them into two steps.

title: Apollo's four powers in the Cratylus
steps: Medicine: ἀπολούων, washing and healing
Mantic: ἁπλοῦς, the simple
Archery: ἀεὶ βάλλων, ever-shooting
Music: ὁμοπολῶν, moving the poles together
note: Socrates' four etymologies, in this order, become the passages between the five steps: cleansing, unmediated knowing, a steady will, and harmonising the many.

title: How awakening typically unfolds
steps: Searching, even on the internet
Signs and synchronicities
Old energies and habits surface to be cleansed
Small tastes of unity, truth revealing itself
note: Her sketch of how people usually live the second and third steps; the glimpses then need a steady will to become a way of life.

title: Three ways to approach a god
steps: External, at the πρόναος: I am here, Apollo is there
Internal, Orphic: Apollo becomes a power of my soul, and I become Apollonian
Central, mysteriac, in the ἄδυτον (?): the god lived as an active mode of being of the One
note: A good first step that objectifies God, then a still dual inner step, then union. All three are true at once and apply to any god, text or idea.

title: How illness descends
steps: Spirit or nous
Soul
Body
note: Greek medicine as she presents it is holistic: illness begins above and descends, so healing starts with purifying vision and the soul.

title: Healing in the Asclepieia
steps: Purification for days beforehand
Incubation (ἐγκοίμησις): sleeping in the sanctuary
Seeing the inner Asclepius
The soul gives the command to heal
note: Healing comes from within, through purified vision: Apollo's first power.

title: Where the quality of eros shows
steps: Our relationship with ourselves
Our intimate partners
Colleagues and every other relationship
Political life and the whole society
note: Eros has shaped our inner relation before it touches anyone else, and its quality then seeps, visibly or invisibly, into every relationship and finally into society.

title: Steering eros toward its goal
steps: Know eros truly and from within, under a wisdom teaching
Apply it with awareness, through the divine nous, not the calculating mind
Turn the rudder of the erotic impulse rightly
Let eros lead where nature set it to lead
Remember the εὖ δαίμων we already are
note: The erotic pedagogy Diotima taught: the goal of eros coincides with the goal of life.
